problem: The trap says the finished stack is taller than n × t (correct) but then concludes that a part built to height H 'may need one extra layer of allowance'. The conclusion runs the wrong way. Because each bonded layer is t plus the glue line, H ÷ t layers would overshoot H; reaching height H needs slightly fewer layers than H ÷ t, never more.
fix: Replace with: 'The glue line makes each bonded layer slightly thicker than t, so the stack is a little taller than n × t. To hit height H exactly, use n = H ÷ (t + glue line) — slightly fewer layers than H ÷ t — and sand the top face for the final allowance.'

problem: 'the cut is the only step that changes shape; the last two steps happen once, after the whole stack is built' is confusing. Removing the excess also changes the shape, and the two clauses are not really connected.
fix: 'The cut alone sets the cross-section of each layer; breaking out the waste and finishing the part happen only once, after the whole stack is built.'

problem: Listing 'simple post-processing' as an advantage sits badly with the text's own account of de-cubing, which is slow manual work and is normally quoted as a disadvantage of LOM.
fix: Say 'no melting, so low shrinkage and no chemical post-curing; post-processing is simple in tools but labour-heavy because de-cubing is done by hand.'

problem: The entry 'one sheet thickness plus the glue line' is a step height (the vertical resolution), not an accuracy or tolerance. Students may then write that LOM's Z accuracy equals 0.1 mm when asked for a tolerance.
fix: Split it: 'Z step (resolution) = t + glue line, about 0.1 mm for 0.1 mm paper; Z tolerance is roughly ± one layer.'
